summary: A manual sweep aimed at language leverage: 24 WebSearch queries (over the usual 10-15, as the owner asked), plus the Italian description search on seven feeds, which found only cross-ING. The first sweep had recorded cross-ING without the Italian it asks for; it is corrected here and still fails on Germany. No role that asks for Italian passed the filters. The closest are a freelancermap Java/Spring Boot/React project for a South Tyrol customer with Italian code comments (dropped: 3-4 days onsite a month) and Moneyfarm's Lead Backend Engineer (Java/Go on AWS, agentic AI tools, Italian required, EUR 65-80k, Milan only); TeamViewer's Italian-speaker implementation role has closed, and Sierra's Italian-speaking agent engineer is in-person in London. Italian employers (Satispay, Moneyfarm, Scalapay) hire engineers only in Milan, the Italian-speaking roles open to Germany are sales or support, and the only shortlist entry is zollsoft's fully remote senior Kotlin/Java role in medical-practice software (7, no Italian). InfoJobs Italia has shut down, Indeed (.de/.it) and StepStone return only listing pages through WebSearch, and the Ashby, Lever and Workable public APIs proved the fastest way to verify; vocab.json is unchanged.
open_questions: Travel ceiling for freelance: the South Tyrol project (Java/Spring Boot/React via Amoria Bond, Italian code comments and API names, 6 months, 4-5 days a week) wants 3-4 days onsite every month, about 9-12 a quarter. Would you take that for a freelance project where Italian is the edge, or does 'a few days a quarter' hold?

Italian employers so far hire engineers in Milan only: Satispay (three office days a week) and Moneyfarm (hybrid, Italian required, Java/Go lead role at EUR 65-80k). Is Milan ever an option (relocation or regular commuting), or are these always not-germany?

The profile counts an Italian employer that can hire from Germany as language leverage, but the schema only marks roles that ask for Italian. Newtwen (remote EU, optional hybrid in Italy, Python) asks for no Italian, so it stays out of the language table. Should 'Italian employer open to Germany' get its own marker?

Freelance long-runners: STINGEL's 100% remote Java/Spring Boot/Kafka project (started 11/2024, runs to 12/2029) is still listed as open on freelancermap. Drop such listings as stale, or keep them while the agency still lists them?

Still open from profile.md: minimum salary and day rate (or 'asked, not stored'), notice period at msg, consultancies as a permanent employer (default down-rank applied to VISION, Academic Work, Intercon, 3Pillar), companies to avoid, and preferred company size.
